newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarians disenchanted with Socialist govt - poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarians disenchanted with Socialist govt - poll.

text.p: Most Bulgarians, plagued by rising prices, shattered banks and looming power rationing in the winter have withdrawn their support for the ruling socialists, an opinion poll showed on Monday.

"Some 67 percent of Bulgaria consider the socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov incapable of governing the country and of dealing with the economic crisis," Andrei Raichev, head of the Bulgarian branch of Gallup International told a news conference.

Videnov came to power in January 1995 after the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), composed largely of communists, regained its grip on power in previous December elections. Polls at that time showed 56 percent support for Videnov.
In a bid to stabilise its crumbling currency and banks Bulgaria hiked annual interest rates to 300 percent and placed one quarter of its banks under central bank supervision.
Of the 1,124 people polled 80 percent said that the situation in the country will deteriorate in the winter.
Bulgaria's anti-communist opposition, helped by the country's deep economic crisis, is so far on course to win the presidential election due on October 27, the poll also showed.
Latest poll results show the opposition's candidate, the lawyer Petar Stoyanov, is well ahead of the BSP candidate culture minister Ivan Marazov.
Some 29 percent of the surveyed said they will back Stoyanov, while 18.6 percent supported Marazov.
